# `sim/particles/ParticleElementRegistry.js`

> **Source:** `engine/sim/particles/ParticleElementRegistry.js`

ParticleElementRegistry.js - Unified Element Registry Bridges the two previously disconnected element systems: - Particle ELEMENTS (fire, water, magic, smoke) from ParticleEmitterSystem.js - Spell SPELL_ELEMENTS (fire, ice, lightning, arcane, nature, dark, holy) from SpellGenerator.js Each unified element defines particle properties (color, materialIndex, temperature, physics modifiers), spell properties (spellColors, effects, damageType), and combination rules (from SpellElementMixer). Also provides bridge functions: - elementMixToEmitterConfig(elements[]) → full emitter config derived from mix - getElementCombination(a, b) → combination result

## Functions

### `setRegistryTrace(enabled, throttleMs = 500)`

Enable or disable element registry trace logging. When enabled, logs every element mix derivation with full pipeline details.

**Parameters:**

- `enabled` *(boolean)* — _No description in source JSDoc._
- `[throttleMs` *(number)* — =500] - Minimum ms between log messages (prevents spam)

### `getRegistryElement(id)`

Get a registry element by ID. Handles backward-compat aliases (e.g., "magic" → "arcane"). Falls back to REACTION_PRODUCTS for byproduct IDs (e.g., "smoke").

**Parameters:**

- `id` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

### `isPrimaryElement(id)`

Check if an element ID is a primary element (user-selectable) vs reaction product.

**Parameters:**

- `id` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

### `getAllRegistryElements()`

Get all registry elements as an array.

### `getRegistryElementsByCategory()`

Get element IDs grouped by category.

**Returns:** >}

### `getElementCombination(elementA, elementB)`

Look up the combination result for two elements.

**Parameters:**

- `elementA` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._
- `elementB` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

**Returns:** Combination data or null if no predefined combo

### `getCombinationsFor(elementId)`

Get all combinations involving a specific element.

**Parameters:**

- `elementId` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

**Returns:** >}

### `elementMixToEmitterConfig(elements)`

Given an array of active element layers [{id, power, enabled}], derive a complete emitter property set: color, colorEnd, temperature, materialIndex, gravityMod, and combination info. This replaces the separate deriveColorFromElements + deriveTemperatureFromElements + deriveMaterialIndexFromElements calls with one unified function.

**Returns:** Derived emitter properties

### `metaSlidersToPhysics(meta)`

Convert meta-slider values (Intensity 0-1, Spread 0-1, Lifetime 0-1) into concrete emitter physics parameters. Used by Simple Mode to provide easy controls.

**Returns:** Physics overrides

### `elementMixToSpellParams(elements)`

Convert an active element mix into spell generator parameters. Used by the "Create Spell From This" button.

**Returns:** }

## Notes & Examples

### Physics Engine Integration

The physics system provides rigid body dynamics, collision detection, and raycasting. Bodies have shapes (box, sphere, mesh), mass properties, and constraints. The GPU physics engine accelerates broad-phase collision detection and particle systems.

**Example: Creating physics bodies**
```js
import { PhysicsWorld } from 'engine/physics/PhysicsWorld.js';
import { RigidBody } from 'engine/physics/RigidBody.js';
import { BoxShape, SphereShape } from 'engine/physics/Shapes.js';

const world = new PhysicsWorld({ gravity: [0, -9.8, 0] });

// Static ground
const ground = new RigidBody({
  type: 'static',
  shape: new BoxShape(10, 1, 10),
  position: [0, -0.5, 0]
});
world.addBody(ground);

// Dynamic box
const box = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  mass: 1,
  shape: new BoxShape(1, 1, 1),
  position: [0, 5, 0],
  restitution: 0.5  // Bounciness
});
world.addBody(box);
```

**Advanced: Collision detection and raycasting**
```js
// Raycast to find what the player is looking at
const hit = world.raycast(camera.position, camera.forward, 100);
if (hit) {
  console.log('Hit entity:', hit.body.entityId);
  console.log('Hit point:', hit.point);
  console.log('Hit normal:', hit.normal);
  
  // Apply impulse at hit point
  hit.body.applyImpulse([0, 10, 0], hit.point);
}

// Shapecast (swept sphere) for character movement
const sweep = world.shapecast(
  player.position,           // Start
  desiredPosition,           // End
  new SphereShape(0.5),    // Player capsule radius
  { ignore: player.body }  // Don't collide with self
);
if (sweep.hit) {
  // Slide along wall
  player.position = sweep.position;
}
```

**Advanced: Constraints and joints**
```js
import { HingeConstraint, FixedConstraint } from 'engine/physics/Constraints.js';

// Door hinge
const doorHinge = new HingeConstraint({
  bodyA: doorFrame,
  bodyB: door,
  pivot: [0, 1, 0],      // Hinge location
  axis: [0, 1, 0],       // Hinge axis (Y up)
  limits: [-90, 90]      // Open angle range in degrees
});
world.addConstraint(doorHinge);

// Ragdoll joint (ball-and-socket)
const shoulder = new FixedConstraint({
  bodyA: torso,
  bodyB: arm,
  pivotA: [0.5, 1.5, 0],  // Shoulder position on torso
  pivotB: [0, 0, 0]       // Shoulder position on arm
});
world.addConstraint(shoulder);
```

**Advanced: Continuous collision detection (CCD)**
```js
// Fast-moving objects need CCD to not tunnel through walls
const projectile = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  shape: new SphereShape(0.1),
  mass: 0.1,
  ccd: { enabled: true, sweptSphereRadius: 0.1 },
  linearDamping: 0  // No air resistance for bullets
});
projectile.velocity = [0, 0, 100];  // Very fast
world.addBody(projectile);
```

**Gotchas:**
- **Units**: Physics uses meters, kilograms, seconds. A 1-unit cube is 1 meter.
- **Time step**: Fixed time step (1/60) gives stable simulation; variable dt causes explosions.
- **Collision layers**: Use collision masks to filter what collides (player vs enemy, bullet vs world).
- **Sleeping**: At-rest bodies sleep to save CPU — wake them before applying forces.
